title: Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — Premium Revision Paper #8

pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the plural of the English word mango? (1 mark)
   A. mangoies
   B. mangos'
   C. mangoss
   D. mangoes

2. What is the plural of the English word loaf? (1 mark)
   A. loaf
   B. loafes
   C. loaves
   D. loafs

3. Which of these is NOT a way of building vocabulary? (1 mark)
   A. Never looking at new words
   B. Making flashcards
   C. Keeping a word bank
   D. Using a dictionary

4. Why is neat handwriting important? (1 mark)
   A. It is only for teachers
   B. It helps the reader to understand the message
   C. It makes the pencil last longer
   D. It makes the book heavier

5. What should a reader do at a full stop? (1 mark)
   A. Skip a line
   B. Pause briefly
   C. Turn the page
   D. Shout

6. Which feeling could a strong, fast voice show? (1 mark)
   A. Sadness
   B. Boredom
   C. Excitement
   D. Sleepiness

7. What should you do to check the punctuation in your paragraph? (1 mark)
   A. Read it aloud and listen for natural pauses
   B. Write it again without looking
   C. Cover it
   D. Tear it

8. How many full stops are needed in: The sky is dark. Rain is coming. (1 mark)
   A. Three
   B. One
   C. Two
   D. None

9. A comma is used to (1 mark)
   A. begin a sentence
   B. show a question
   C. end a story
   D. separate items in a list

10. Which is a verb in: The pot tipped over? (1 mark)
   A. tipped
   B. over
   C. The
   D. pot

11. A good storyteller (1 mark)
   A. forgets the ending
   B. reads without looking
   C. practises and speaks clearly
   D. whispers all the time

12. What is the difference between a proverb and a story? (1 mark)
   A. A proverb is a short saying and a story is longer with events
   B. They are the same
   C. A story is shorter
   D. A proverb has many characters

13. What does the proverb Look before you leap advise a writer of a story about a careless pupil? (1 mark)
   A. Never look
   B. Run fast
   C. Think before acting
   D. Be careless

14. Why should you plan before writing a story? (1 mark)
   A. To organise your ideas
   B. To finish early
   C. To make it longer
   D. To avoid a title

15. What is a service? (1 mark)
   A. Work done for others
   B. A market
   C. A thing you can hold
   D. A kind of coin

16. What is a vocabulary bank? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of poem
   B. A place for money
   C. A list of useful words on a theme
   D. A book cover

17. What should you do if a stranger promises cheap goods and asks for money first? (1 mark)
   A. Send money at once
   B. Trust them
   C. Give your address
   D. Be careful and ask an adult

18. What does a preposition show? (1 mark)
   A. The price of goods
   B. The position of one thing in relation to another
   C. The sound of an animal
   D. The colour of a thing

19. Which of these is a preposition? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. banana
   C. behind
   D. jump

20. What should you do while a classmate recites? (1 mark)
   A. Laugh
   B. Leave
   C. Talk
   D. Listen and respect them

21. What is creative writing? (1 mark)
   A. Copying a text exactly
   B. Writing only numbers
   C. Using imagination to write stories, poems and other pieces
   D. Writing a list of names

22. What is leisure time? (1 mark)
   A. Lesson time
   B. Sleeping time
   C. Exam time
   D. Free time when you are not working or in class

23. What is an interjection? (1 mark)
   A. A word that joins sentences
   B. A short word that shows a sudden feeling
   C. A word that shows position
   D. A word that names a thing

24. What is a debate? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of poem
   B. A game of football
   C. A song
   D. A discussion in which two sides give opposite views with reasons

25. Why are interjections used more in speech than in formal writing? (1 mark)
   A. They are illegal in writing
   B. They show quick feelings in speech
   C. They are long
   D. They are difficult

26. In the kite passage, what went wrong? (1 mark)
   A. The children fell
   B. The string broke
   C. The wind stopped
   D. The kite flew away forever

27. Which is NOT a feeling shown by interjections? (1 mark)
   A. The price of an item
   B. Joy
   C. Disgust
   D. Pain

28. In a script dialogue, what comes straight after the speaker's name? (1 mark)
   A. A colon
   B. A number
   C. A bracket
   D. A full stop

29. Why do writers use interjections in dialogues? (1 mark)
   A. To make it longer
   B. To show feelings and make speech natural
   C. To fill the page
   D. To hide the story

30. Which is the last part of a telephone conversation? (1 mark)
   A. Greeting
   B. Asking for a favour
   C. Giving your name
   D. Saying goodbye

31. Why do we match devices to their uses? (1 mark)
   A. To break them
   B. To hide them
   C. To know what each is for
   D. To lose them

32. Why should you ask permission before using someone's phone? (1 mark)
   A. It is a game
   B. It is illegal to touch phones
   C. Phones never break
   D. It belongs to them and needs care

33. What should you not do with an advert that asks for money from strangers? (1 mark)
   A. Send money without asking an adult
   B. Check the facts
   C. Read it carefully
   D. Ask an adult

34. What does N/A mean? (1 mark)
   A. Not applicable
   B. New address
   C. No answer always
   D. Next assignment

35. What is the purpose of the instructions on a form? (1 mark)
   A. To make it hard
   B. To use up space
   C. To hide the title
   D. To tell you how to fill it in

36. Where should your class keep collected forms? (1 mark)
   A. In a portfolio
   B. Under a stone
   C. In the fire
   D. In the river

37. What is polite when you want to speak in a discussion? (1 mark)
   A. Shout
   B. Stand on a chair
   C. Snatch the talking stick
   D. Raise your hand or signal

38. What is repetition in a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Deleting lines
   B. Changing the title
   C. Repeating words or lines for effect
   D. Adding a picture

39. Which is a signal word for the second step? (1 mark)
   A. Yesterday
   B. Never
   C. Finally
   D. Next

40. Which is a poor instruction? (1 mark)
   A. Wet your hands
   B. Rinse the soap
   C. Do the thing with the papers
   D. Collect the exercise books and place them on the table

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Join the sentences with when: I counted my money. The bell rang. (2 marks)

42. Mama Neema buys a box of bananas for 200 shillings and sells it for 260 shillings. Find her profit. (2 marks)

43. Explain the difference between a simile and a metaphor and give an example of each. (4 marks)

44. List the six elements of a story. (3 marks)

45. Copy this sentence correctly: the food is hot (2 marks)

46. Give three rules of good telephone manners. (3 marks)

47. Give three rules for good turn taking. (3 marks)

48. Complete with a simile: The baby slept like a ______. (2 marks)

49. Describe how a class can collect and keep cultural songs from the community. (4 marks)

50. What is a paragraph and what is its main idea? (2 marks)

51. Give three questions you can ask when studying a picture. (3 marks)

52. Explain what attentive listening means. (2 marks)

53. Put the steps in order: (a) Finally, serve. (b) First, boil water. (c) Next, add tea leaves. (3 marks)

54. Explain what the proverb Honesty is the best policy means. (2 marks)

55. Write a five-sentence oral paragraph about a free day. Include three interjections that show different feelings. (5 marks)

56. Explain how the position game is played with objects on a table. (4 marks)

57. Give three signal words used to show the order of steps. (3 marks)

58. Compose a four-line poem about a good leader. Make lines two and four rhyme. (4 marks)

59. State three steps for building vocabulary from a text. (3 marks)

60. Give two conjunctions used to join sentences. (2 marks)

61. Explain what intonation is and give one English example of a rising voice. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — mangoes
   Mango takes es in the plural, mangoes.

2. C — loaves
   Loaf changes f to ves in the plural.

3. A — Never looking at new words
   Ignoring new words does not build vocabulary.

4. B — It helps the reader to understand the message
   A message is useful only if it can be read.

5. B — Pause briefly
   Full stops tell us to pause.

6. C — Excitement
   Excitement is often read faster and stronger.

7. A — Read it aloud and listen for natural pauses
   Reading aloud helps find where pauses and stops belong.

8. C — Two
   There are two sentences, so two full stops.

9. D — separate items in a list
   Commas separate list items and show short pauses.

10. A — tipped
   Tipped shows what the pot did.

11. C — practises and speaks clearly
   Practice and clarity make a good teller.

12. A — A proverb is a short saying and a story is longer with events
   Proverbs are very short.

13. C — Think before acting
   It would fit a story where carelessness causes trouble.

14. A — To organise your ideas
   A plan gives your story a clear shape.

15. A — Work done for others
   Cutting hair is a service.

16. C — A list of useful words on a theme
   A word bank stores words to learn.

17. D — Be careful and ask an adult
   Such offers may be tricks.

18. B — The position of one thing in relation to another
   Prepositions show position such as on, under and beside.

19. C — behind
   Behind shows position.

20. D — Listen and respect them
   Good listeners respect performers.

21. C — Using imagination to write stories, poems and other pieces
   Creative writing is imaginative.

22. D — Free time when you are not working or in class
   Leisure is free time.

23. B — A short word that shows a sudden feeling
   Interjections show emotion.

24. D — A discussion in which two sides give opposite views with reasons
   A debate is an organised argument of a motion.

25. B — They show quick feelings in speech
   Formal writing usually uses full sentences.

26. B — The string broke
   The string broke and the kite fell.

27. A — The price of an item
   Interjections show feelings, not prices.

28. A — A colon
   The name is followed by a colon.

29. B — To show feelings and make speech natural
   Interjections show emotions.

30. D — Saying goodbye
   Calls end with a goodbye.

31. C — To know what each is for
   Knowing the use helps us choose the right device.

32. D — It belongs to them and needs care
   Respecting others' property is polite.

33. A — Send money without asking an adult
   Never send money to strangers.

34. A — Not applicable
   N/A means the question does not apply.

35. D — To tell you how to fill it in
   Instructions guide the person filling it.

36. A — In a portfolio
   A portfolio keeps them organised.

37. D — Raise your hand or signal
   Signal politely.

38. C — Repeating words or lines for effect
   Repetition emphasises an idea.

39. D — Next
   Next shows the following step.

40. C — Do the thing with the papers
   It is vague.

SECTION B
----
41. (2 marks)
   Answer: When I counted my money, the bell rang.
   Working / marking points: One mark for using when and one mark for the comma.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: 260 minus 200 equals 60 shillings.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the working and one mark for the answer with units.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: A simile compares using like or as, for example as quick as lightning. A metaphor says one thing is another, for example Time is money.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each definition and one for each example.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending.
   Working / marking points: Award 3 marks for all six, 2 marks for four or five, and 1 mark for two or three.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: The food is hot.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the capital letter and one mark for the full stop.

46. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet, give your name, speak clearly, do not interrupt, do not call late without a reason, say goodbye.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

47. (3 marks)
   Answer: Wait for the speaker to finish, keep your turn short, do not always speak first, listen politely.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each rule.

48. (2 marks)
   Answer: log (or a stone, or any suitable comparison)
   Working / marking points: One mark for a suitable comparison and one for keeping like.

49. (4 marks)
   Answer: Ask elders politely, listen carefully, write or record the song with permission, note the name of the person who shared it and the date, and store it in a class portfolio.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four correct steps.

50. (2 marks)
   Answer: A paragraph is a group of sentences about one topic. The main idea is what it is mostly about.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each part.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Who is there, where are they, what are they doing, why, what happens next.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

52. (2 marks)
   Answer: Attentive listening means choosing to give your eyes, ears and mind to the speaker so that you understand and remember what is said.
   Working / marking points: One mark for choosing to pay attention and one mark for understanding or remembering.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: b, c, a
   Working / marking points: One mark for each correct position.

54. (2 marks)
   Answer: Telling the truth is always the wisest choice because it builds trust.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for the reason.

55. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five sentences with three suitable interjections such as Hurray, Wow and Oops used to show joy, surprise and a mistake.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence and one mark for three suitable interjections shown correctly.

56. (4 marks)
   Answer: One pupil gives an instruction such as put the pencil on the book. Another follows it. The class checks whether the position is correct. Then the roles are swapped.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

57. (3 marks)
   Answer: first, next, then, after that, finally (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

58. (4 marks)
   Answer: Any four-line poem on leadership with two rhyming lines, for example A good leader listens, Speaks the truth each day, Helps the weak and lonely, And shows the proper way.
   Working / marking points: Two marks for theme and four lines, two marks for rhyme.

59. (3 marks)
   Answer: Read once for meaning, underline new words, write them on flashcards with meanings, use each in a sentence (any three).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each step.

60. (2 marks)
   Answer: and, but, or, so (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark each.

61. (2 marks)
   Answer: Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice as we speak. A question such as Are you coming? rises at the end.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one mark for a correct example.
